notes: All 6 required web searches ran this time, plus 1 extra search on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act cosponsors (7 in total). Searches on superintelligence, extinction, pause and China mostly returned Speaker Mike Johnson; one news item (san.com / Axios coverage of 'Johnson' calling for an AI industry meeting and safeguards against AI advancing beyond human control) is about Speaker Mike Johnson, not Julie Johnson, and is not attributed to her. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: the House version is H.R. 10538; the FastDemocracy tracker (https://fastdemocracy.com/bill-search/us/119/bills/USB00108512/) lists 12 cosponsors and she is not among them; congress.gov returned HTTP 403, so this was not confirmed there. The statement quote was read through a summarizing fetch tool on the official page; a reviewer should confirm the exact wording. A LegiStorm mirror of the same release, seen only in a search summary, attributes to her: 'I've led on election reform my entire career, and artificial intelligence is the next major challenge we must confront.' This was not read at source and is left out. Her AI issue page (https://juliejohnson.house.gov/issues/artificial-intelligence-ai) is undated; it says AI 'should not replace workers-it should empower them' and calls for 'a smart, balanced regulatory framework' protecting the public and children (would be level D; not entered as a statement because undated). The earlier attempt opened press release listing pages 1-3 (April 2026 back to December 2025); pages 4-9 were not checked. Multi-signer House letters were not searched, as instructed.
